headline: Monday Night Football: Chargers edge Ravens 23-20 as Jim Harbaugh tops John in brotherly clash
teaser: Justin Herbert runs for a 22-yard touchdown, rookie Omarion Hampton rushes for 105 yards, and Tarheeb Still forces a late fumble on Zay Flowers to seal a 23-20 road triumph for Los Angeles.
story:
Jim Harbaugh secured bragging rights in the family rivalry on Monday night, 16 November, as his Los Angeles Chargers held off John Harbaugh and the Baltimore Ravens for a gritty 23-20 road victory at M&T Bank Stadium.

Justin Herbert set the tone early for the visitors, scrambling out of pressure and diving inside the pylon for a 22-yard touchdown run to give Los Angeles a lead they would never surrender. Rookie running back Omarion Hampton delivered a breakout prime-time performance, pounding Baltimore's front seven for 105 yards on 21 carries, including a physical 4-yard touchdown plunge in the third quarter.

Lamar Jackson rallied the Ravens in the fourth quarter, connecting with Mark Andrews on a 14-yard touchdown pass to pull within three points. But with Baltimore driving into field goal range in the final two minutes, Chargers cornerback Tarheeb Still punched the ball loose from Zay Flowers, allowing Los Angeles to recover and run out the clock to improve to 7-3.
whyCareReason: Jim Harbaugh edges John Harbaugh in the second official coaching clash between brothers, earning Los Angeles a pivotal tiebreaker in the AFC playoff race.
stakes: The Chargers (7-3) cement their position in the AFC wild card race while the Ravens (7-3) lose critical ground in the AFC North.
rivalryAngle: First meeting between Jim and John Harbaugh since Super Bowl XLVII in New Orleans, with Jim claiming his first head-to-head NFL win over his older brother.
funFacts: The Chargers outrushed the Ravens 160 yards to 16, holding Derrick Henry to just 12 rushing yards.
Justin Herbert recorded his first career 20-plus-yard rushing touchdown on Monday Night Football.
Tarheeb Still's fourth-quarter forced fumble was his third turnover created in the last four games.
